events.title: Google announced Blink rendering engine
events.summary: On April 3, 2013, Google announced [Blink] — a fork of [WebKit] that would power Chrome and Opera, splitting the open-source browser engine landscape.
events.about: [Blink] let Google iterate faster than [WebKit]'s multi-vendor governance — dropping vendor prefixes, changing architecture, and eventually dominating [Chromium]-based browsers. Safari kept [WebKit]; Chrome, Edge, Opera, and most mobile browsers adopted [Blink].

narrative.whyChosen: [Blink] fork was the inflection point toward [Chromium] engine monoculture.
narrative.whyImportant: It ended the [WebKit]-only era outside Firefox and defined modern browser internals.
narrative.problemSolved: Google needed engine freedom to ship multi-process architecture and rapid web platform changes.

events.title: Samsung Galaxy S4 released
events.summary: Samsung began selling the Samsung Galaxy S4 — 1080p five-inch display and eye-tracking features — peak TouchWiz era dominance.
events.about: The Galaxy S series remained [Android]'s volume flagship counterweight to iPhone. 1080p five-inch display and eye-tracking features — peak touchwiz era dominance. Developers testing [Android] builds routinely validated on Galaxy S hardware as the default non-[Pixel] reference.

narrative.whyChosen: The Samsung Galaxy S4 continued Samsung's annual [Android] flagship cadence.
narrative.whyImportant: Galaxy S devices set the hardware bar millions of [Android] users and developers encounter.
narrative.problemSolved: [Android] needed consistent premium hardware for testing flagship features each year.
